shared.name: on

Activation.name: Activation
Activation.summary: When a tab opens as the arrow keys move over it.

variants.name: Automatic
variants.doc: Moving to a tab opens it: the default, right when the panels are ready at once.

variants.name: Manual
variants.doc: Moving only moves focus; Enter or Space opens the tab. Right when opening one is slow, such as a panel loaded from the server.

ActivityFeed.name: ActivityFeed
ActivityFeed.summary: What people did lately, newest first.

constructors.name: new
constructors.args: id: impl Into<String>, title: impl Into<Node>
constructors.doc: A feed with this `id`, called `title`. The id builds the ids of the list, the notice and the empty message.

constructors.name: rows
constructors.args: items: impl IntoIterator<Item = ActivityItem>, offset_seconds: i32
constructors.doc: Just the rows, with no header and no list: what the source of a live feed answers with, to be added at the top of the feed's list. `offset_seconds` is the feed's own time zone offset, so a clock time reads the same in a row that arrives later.

methods.name: live
methods.doc: Shows the live dot. It says "Connecting" in grey until a stream is open, then "Live" in green; "Reconnecting" in amber while it comes back; "Paused" while the page is hidden; and "Not live" when the stream refused for good. Without the runtime it is not shown.

methods.name: summary
methods.doc: Writes one line under the title: "10:30 to 11:30 · 14 events".

methods.name: period
methods.doc: Puts any control at the end of the header: a period select, a switch.

methods.name: period_select
methods.args: action: impl Into<Href>, region_id: &str, select: NativeSelect
methods.doc: Puts a period select at the end of the header. Choosing an option asks `action` for the page again with the choice in the query (`?window=15`) and morphs the region `region_id` in place; with JavaScript off, an Apply button does the same as a plain form. Give the region's source the same choice, so a live feed keeps to the period. `select` needs a name and an `aria-label`.

methods.name: item
methods.doc: Adds a row.

methods.name: items
methods.doc: Adds rows.

methods.name: time_zone
methods.doc: Sets the zone the clock times are shown in, by name and offset from UTC in seconds, and writes "Times in Asia/Kolkata (GMT+05:30)" under the title.

methods.name: height
methods.doc: Sets how tall the list grows before it scrolls.

methods.name: heading
methods.doc: Sets the level of the title. The default is 3.

methods.name: labels
methods.doc: Replaces the words.

methods.name: loading
methods.doc: Shows placeholder rows: the first load is on its way.

methods.name: failed
methods.doc: Says the rows couldn't be loaded, keeping the header so the reader can still change the period.

methods.name: retry
methods.doc: Adds a "Try again" link to a failed feed.

methods.name: empty
methods.doc: Sets what shows when there are no rows.

methods.name: list_id
methods.doc: The id of the list that rows are added to: a `Region`'s feed target.

methods.name: empty_id
methods.doc: The id of the empty message, which a feed removes when the first row comes.

methods.name: in_region
methods.args: region_id: &str, src: impl Into<Href>, stream: impl Into<super::Live>, cursor: impl Into<String>
methods.doc: Wraps the feed in a `Region` that fetches new rows from `src` (with `after=<cursor>`) whenever `stream` speaks, and adds them at the top: a stream's address, or names on the app's live hub (`LiveStream::on`). `cursor` is the newest row's cursor. The feed shows its live dot.

ActivityItem.name: ActivityItem
ActivityItem.summary: One row of a feed: who did what.

methods.name: object

methods.name: tag

methods.name: tone

methods.name: icon

methods.name: at
methods.doc: Says when, in unix seconds. The feed prints the clock time in its zone.

methods.name: time_text
methods.doc: Prints this instead of the clock time: "2 min ago".

methods.name: meta
methods.doc: Adds a fact on the meta line: a browser, a place, an email.

methods.name: metas
methods.doc: Adds several facts.

methods.name: href
methods.doc: Makes the actor a link and the whole row a click target. Point it at a page or at a page that opens a `Sheet`.

methods.name: muted
methods.doc: Quieter, for work a machine did.

methods.name: filtered
methods.doc: Leaves it out until the reader ticks the notice that says some rows were hidden. It is still in the page.

methods.name: id
methods.doc: Sets its `id`. A row whose id is already on the page is not added again when a live feed brings it a second time.

AppFont.name: AppFont
AppFont.summary: A typeface of the app's own: one woff2 file, compiled in with `include_bytes!`, served at `/_navree/ui/app/{name}-{hash}.woff2` as `immutable`, with the `@font-face` rule that names it. See the module.

constructors.name: new
constructors.args: name: &'static str, family: &'static str, bytes: &'static [u8], most: usize
constructors.doc: The woff2 file `bytes`, named `name` (1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits and `-`), for the CSS family `family` (letters, digits, spaces and `-`, at most 64), at most `most` bytes long. A file that isn't woff2, past its ceiling, or a name or family of anything else, fails the app's build. Regular weight, upright, `font-display: swap` and preloaded until you say otherwise.

methods.name: weight
methods.doc: Its weight: `600` for a semibold file.

methods.name: weights
methods.doc: The weights a variable file covers: `weights(100, 900)`.

methods.name: italic
methods.doc: An italic file.

methods.name: display
methods.doc: What the browser does while the font loads (`swap` by default).

methods.name: lazy
methods.doc: Leaves the file out of the page's head as a preload: a font only some pages use is fetched when the text that needs it is drawn.

methods.name: name
methods.doc: Its name.

methods.name: family
methods.doc: The CSS family it is called.

methods.name: bytes
methods.doc: The font file.

methods.name: preloads
methods.doc: Whether a page preloads it.

methods.name: url
methods.doc: Where the file is served: `/_navree/ui/app/{name}-{hash}.woff2`.

methods.name: face_url
methods.doc: Where its `@font-face` rule is served: `/_navree/ui/app/{name}.face-{hash}.css`.

methods.name: face
methods.doc: The `@font-face` rule: the family, the file's address, the weights, the style and the display.

AppPage.name: AppPage
AppPage.summary: A page in the shell: what a handler returns.

methods.name: topbar
methods.doc: Puts `node` in the middle of the top bar for this page: what belongs to the page and the request, such as a pager between days that depends on the day shown. It stands centred in the bar, between the navigation and the bar's own controls, and stays on phones.

methods.name: document_title
methods.doc: Sets the title the browser's tab shows, in place of the heading: a page headed with a greeting is titled by what it is. The shell's title template still applies.

methods.name: appearance
methods.doc: Sets how this page looks, in place of what the app, the workspace and the reader chose: a preview, say.

methods.name: layout
methods.doc: Sets where this page's navigation stands, in place of the app's layout.

methods.name: density
methods.doc: Sets this page's density, in place of its theme's.

methods.name: theme_sheet
methods.doc: Links the stylesheet of a theme of your own that a part of the page is drawn in. See `View::theme_sheet`.

methods.name: stylesheet
methods.doc: Links a stylesheet of the app's own on this page, after the shell's. See `View::stylesheet`.

methods.name: font
methods.doc: Links a typeface of the app's own on this page, after the shell's. See `View::font`.

methods.name: current_appearance
methods.doc: The appearance the page is drawn in.

methods.name: status
methods.doc: Sets the status the page answers with (`200` by default): the status of an error page drawn in the shell.

methods.name: crumb
methods.args: label: impl Into<Cow<'static, str>>, href: impl Into<Href>
methods.doc: Adds a step to the breadcrumb, before this page.

methods.name: prefetch_crumbs
methods.doc: Fetches the breadcrumb's links when the pointer rests on one or it takes focus. Off unless asked, as for every link.

methods.name: actions
methods.doc: Adds actions beside the page's heading.

methods.name: body
methods.doc: Adds to the page.

methods.name: to_view
methods.doc: The whole document.

AppSheet.name: AppSheet
AppSheet.summary: A stylesheet of the app's own, compiled in with `include_bytes!` and served by the toolkit at `/_navree/ui/app/{name}-{hash}.css` as `immutable`. See the module.

constructors.name: new
constructors.doc: The stylesheet `bytes`, named `name` (1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits and `-`), at most `most` bytes long. A sheet past its ceiling, or a name of anything else, fails the app's build.

methods.name: name
methods.doc: Its name.

methods.name: bytes
methods.doc: The stylesheet.

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: The first 12 hex digits of its content hash, as the toolkit's own files carry.

methods.name: url
methods.doc: Where it is served: `/_navree/ui/app/{name}-{hash}.css`.

AppShell.name: AppShell
AppShell.summary: The app's `Shell`, applied to this request: which link is active, whether the sidebar is collapsed, a toast left for this page.

methods.name: page
methods.doc: A page titled `title`.

methods.name: workspace
methods.doc: Sets what the workspace chose, from the app's store: it lies over the app's default, and when locked the reader can't change its theme.

methods.name: user_theme
methods.doc: Sets what the reader chose, from the app's store, in place of the cookie. A theme set here is the app's word: it needn't be one the shell offers.

methods.name: user_menu
methods.doc: Sets the user at the foot of the sidebar for this request, in place of the shell's: the person signed in, with what they may do. The app's one shell stays as it is.

methods.name: header_slot
methods.doc: Puts `slot` in the sidebar's header for this request, in place of the shell's `header_slot`: the switcher of the workspace this request is in.

methods.name: csrf
methods.doc: Sets the session's CSRF token, which the shell's own forms (the user menu's actions, the theme menu) carry with JavaScript off, in place of the token the request's cookie holds: for a module that reads it from the session.

methods.name: appearance
methods.doc: How this request's pages look: the app's default, then the workspace's, then the reader's (the app's store, else the cookie), then `?theme=` and `?mode=`. A locked workspace keeps its theme; the mode is still the reader's.

Appearance.name: Appearance
Appearance.summary: A theme and a mode: how a page looks.

constructors.name: new
constructors.doc: `theme` in `mode`.

constructors.name: parse
constructors.doc: Reads `to_value`'s text. A theme of your own comes back with the id `custom`; match it to yours by `Theme::key`.

methods.name: theme
methods.doc: The theme.

methods.name: mode
methods.doc: The mode.

methods.name: with_theme
methods.doc: The same with another theme.

methods.name: with_mode
methods.doc: The same with another mode.

methods.name: to_value
methods.doc: The text to store for it, in a column or a cookie: `dark.ocean`. `Appearance::parse` reads it back.

methods.name: for_reader
methods.doc: This look with the reader's own choice laid over it: the theme and mode kept in the cookie that the theme menu and the theme toggle set, then `?theme=` and `?mode=` in `query`, which last for this request only. For a page outside the app shell, such as a public site's, whose `AppShell` would do this for it.

methods.name: is_default
methods.doc: Whether this is what a page gets with nothing set: the default theme, dark.

ApprovalCard.name: ApprovalCard

Chart.name: Chart
Chart.summary: A chart of lines, areas or bars over one x: categories, times or numbers.

constructors.name: line
constructors.doc: Lines: change over time, several series side by side.

constructors.name: area
constructors.doc: Areas: a line with a wash under it; stacked, parts of a total over time.

constructors.name: bar
constructors.doc: Bars from one baseline: compare amounts. Several series sit side by side.

methods.name: horizontal
methods.doc: Bars lie along rows, a label on each: for long names and ranked lists.

methods.name: stacked
methods.doc: Stacks the series: bars on bars, areas on areas.

methods.name: stacked_percent
methods.doc: Stacks the series as shares of each x's total, to 100%.

methods.name: smooth
methods.doc: Draws lines as a monotone curve, which never overshoots a value: the same as `.curve(Curve::Monotone)`.

methods.name: curve
methods.doc: How lines and areas run between points: straight, a monotone curve, or steps.

methods.name: dots
methods.doc: Which points of a line show a dot: the last (the default), all, or none.

methods.name: active_dot
methods.doc: The dot that marks the value under the pointer or the keys.

methods.name: x_axis
methods.doc: What the x axis draws: its labels (the default), its line, its tick marks. `Axis::hidden` gives the plot the room the labels took.

methods.name: y_axis
methods.doc: What the value axis draws: its labels (the default), its line, its tick marks. `Axis::hidden` gives the plot the room the labels took.

methods.name: grid
methods.doc: The gridlines behind the marks: across at each value tick by default.

methods.name: x_ticks
methods.doc: Which x labels are written: every n-th, at most n, the first and the last.

methods.name: y_domain
methods.doc: The range of the value axis: from the data, padded, or fixed.

methods.name: y_categories
methods.doc: Names the values of the value axis: value 0 is `names[0]`, 1 is `names[1]`. Each name is a tick, the axis runs from the first to the last, and the table and the tooltip write the name, not the number: for states such as sleep stages, with `Curve::Step`.

methods.name: lanes
methods.doc: Gives each of the named values a lane of its own: the axis runs half a step past the first and the last, so each name sits in the middle of its band, and an area fills down to the foot of the lowest lane. A stepped area over sleep stages then shows the lowest stage (deep sleep) as an area like the others, not as a line along the foot of the plot.

methods.name: baseline
methods.doc: Bars grow from `value`, up for a value above it and down for one below, rather than from zero: years from an age, degrees from a normal temperature, a score against a reference. A line is drawn at the level, and the value axis holds it and the values without reaching down to zero, so a domain such as `Domain::fixed(18, 60)` is kept. Bars side by side only: a stack still grows from zero. The table and the tooltip say the values as they are.

methods.name: reference
methods.doc: Adds a reference line: a level, an average, a zero baseline, the diagonal.

methods.name: zone
methods.doc: Adds a band of the value axis, shaded behind the data: a target zone.

methods.name: tooltip
methods.doc: What the tooltip shows.

methods.name: detail
methods.args: name: impl Into<String>, texts: impl IntoIterator<Item = S>
methods.doc: Adds a column of words, one for each x: in the table after the series, and as a line of the tooltip (`Duration`, `23 min`).

methods.name: motion
methods.doc: How the marks come in: lines draw from the start, bars grow from the baseline, dots pop in. Off by default; always off for a reader who asks for less motion.

methods.name: categories
methods.doc: Named categories along x.

methods.name: times
methods.doc: Times along x, as wall-clock times in the zone the data was counted in.

methods.name: days
methods.doc: Days along x.

methods.name: numbers
methods.doc: Numbers along x.

methods.name: grain
methods.doc: The period each time stands for, which sets how it reads: an hour reads `14:00`, a month `Nov 2026`. Found from the spacing of the times when not set.

methods.name: x_label
methods.doc: The table's first column: what x is.

methods.name: series
methods.doc: Adds a series. Colours follow the order series are added in.

methods.name: series_list
methods.doc: Adds several series.

methods.name: format
methods.doc: How values are written: on the axis, in the tooltip and in the table.

methods.name: y_min
methods.doc: The value axis starts here at most.

methods.name: y_max
methods.doc: The value axis ends here at least.

methods.name: y_zero
methods.doc: Whether a line's value axis starts at zero (it does by default; bars always do).

methods.name: y_ticks
methods.doc: About how many ticks the value axis writes.

methods.name: annotation
methods.doc: Adds a target, an event or a band.

methods.name: height
methods.doc: The plot's height in pixels, 60 to 800 (200 by default). The x labels add 22.

methods.name: max_points
methods.doc: The most points a line or an area draws (640 by default, at least 16): more are reduced with largest-triangle-three-buckets.

methods.name: max_bars
methods.doc: The most bars (120 by default, at least 4): times and numbers past it merge their neighbours, categories fold their tail into Other.

methods.name: merge
methods.doc: How merged bars combine.

methods.name: drill
methods.doc: Makes each category or period a link, `links[i]` for the i-th: where its rows are listed, such as a `DataTable` filtered to that day. Each bar of a vertical bar chart is a link named by its series and its period, and the name of the period in the chart's table is one too, which a keyboard and a screen reader reach. When bars are merged or a line is thinned, a row stands for several values and has no link. A link must stay on this site; a `Report::drill_links` builds the links for a report's periods.

methods.name: toggles
methods.doc: Makes the legend a set of switches that hide and show each series, with or without JavaScript. Not for stacked charts, whose stacks would lose a layer.

DataTable.name: DataTable
DataTable.summary: A table with search, filters, sort links, selection and pagination, as one region.

constructors.name: new
constructors.args: id: &'static str, query: &'a TableQuery<R, F>, data: impl Into<TableData<'a, R>>
constructors.doc: The rows of this page; `id` names the region.

methods.name: cell
methods.args: name: &'static str, draw: impl Fn(&R) -> N + 'a
methods.doc: Draws column `name` from the whole row, into anything that becomes a `Node`: a badge, an avatar, a list of tags, an `EditCell`. Files and labels still read the field's plain text. `#[col(cell = path)]` is the same in the definition; this form can use what the page knows, such as permissions.

methods.name: live
methods.doc: Refetches the table this often while the page is visible, and shows that it's live, with a button to refresh now. Typing, focus, open menus and the selection are kept; a reply that a newer change overtook is dropped.

methods.name: live_from
methods.doc: Refetches the table whenever this server-sent event stream says something.

methods.name: debounce
methods.doc: How long typing in the search or a text filter waits for a pause before the table asks again: 100 ms unless this says otherwise, up to 5 s. A tick or a choice applies at once. A longer wait suits a search the database is slow to answer.

methods.name: prefetch
methods.doc: Fetches the table's own links (sort, page, filter chips, details) when the pointer rests on one or it takes focus, so the next state is often there before the click. Off unless asked. They change nothing, but each fetch costs a page of rows; a cell's own link, such as a row's page, is never fetched this way.

methods.name: live_event
methods.doc: Listens for the stream's events called `name` instead of its unnamed ones. See `Region::live_event`.

methods.name: live_on
methods.doc: Refetches the table whenever its stream says one of its names: the app's live hub (`LiveStream::on`) or any stream on this site. See `Region::live_on`.

methods.name: refreshable
methods.doc: Adds a button that refetches the table.

methods.name: filter_bar
methods.doc: Puts the filters in a bar over the table, where each user can pick which show and in what order. A filter holding a value always shows.

methods.name: total

methods.name: empty

methods.name: caption
methods.doc: Names the table for assistive technology.

methods.name: labels

methods.name: filter_row

methods.name: height

methods.name: sticky_header

methods.name: bleed

methods.name: scroll_to

methods.name: keyboard_grid

methods.name: failed

methods.name: loading

methods.name: bulk

methods.name: without_select_all_matching

methods.name: selectable_if
methods.doc: Which rows can be ticked. Others show a disabled box. "Select all results" isn't offered, since no count of the selectable rows exists.

methods.name: csrf

methods.name: row_actions
methods.doc: Adds a menu to each row.

methods.name: row_href
methods.doc: Makes a click anywhere on a row, outside its controls, go here.

methods.name: sticky_rows

methods.name: detail
methods.doc: What a row opens to. Only open rows are drawn: `open=` is in the URL.

methods.name: export

variants.name: ThisMonth

DateRangePicker.summary: A range of days from two dates: one button, and a popover with presets beside a calendar of two months.

methods.name: min
methods.doc: The earliest day that can be chosen.

methods.name: max
methods.doc: The latest day that can be chosen.

methods.name: locale
methods.doc: Names and orders the days after a language and region.

methods.name: today

methods.name: min_days
methods.doc: The fewest days a range may hold.

methods.name: max_days
methods.doc: The most days a range may hold.

methods.name: placeholder
methods.doc: The words on the button while no range is chosen.

methods.name: title
methods.doc: A title shown on the button before the range, such as "Created".

methods.name: not_clearable
methods.doc: Leaves out the button that empties the picker.

methods.name: confirm

methods.name: disabled

DateRangeQuery.name: DateRangeQuery
DateRangeQuery.summary: A range as it arrives in a query string, before it is checked. Axum-style extractors fill it from `?from=2026-11-01&to=2026-11-03`.

methods.name: range
methods.doc: The range, when both ends are dates. A pair in the wrong order is put right; anything else is no range, never an error.

methods.doc: The range held to `limits`: `Ok(None)` when there is no range (an end is missing or not a date), `Ok(Some(range))` when there is one the limits allow, and the reason in `Err` when there is one they refuse. The same `RangeRules` the picker was given, so what the browser held a person to is what the server holds the request to.

methods.name: range_within
methods.doc: The range, when it is one the limits allow; no range when it is not (a page that would rather show its default window than an error).

DateRules.name: DateRules
DateRules.summary: The days a calendar will not let a person choose.

constructors.name: new
constructors.doc: Rules that allow every day.

methods.name: min
methods.doc: The earliest day that can be chosen.

methods.name: max
methods.doc: The latest day that can be chosen.

methods.name: disable_weekdays
methods.doc: Turns weekdays off.

methods.name: disable_dates
methods.doc: Turns single days off.

methods.name: disable_range
methods.doc: Turns a run of days off, both ends included. Given backwards, it is put right.

methods.args: rule: impl Fn(NaiveDate) -> bool + Send + Sync + 'static
methods.doc: Turns off every day the function answers `true` for. The calendar asks it for the days it can show (three years around the month it opens on) and stops navigation at the edges of that window; the server asks it for each date that comes back.

methods.name: earliest
methods.doc: The earliest day, when set.

methods.name: latest
methods.doc: The latest day, when set.

methods.name: has_rule
methods.doc: Whether a rule function is set.

methods.doc: Why `day` can't be chosen, or `Ok` when it can.

methods.name: allows
methods.doc: Whether `day` can be chosen.

methods.name: check_range
methods.doc: Why `range` can't be chosen: an end that is off, a day between that is off, or a length outside `min_days` and `max_days`. The same check the browser makes as a range is picked.

methods.name: blocks_span
methods.doc: Whether any day from `from` to `to` can't be chosen. The limits, the weekdays, the listed days and the listed runs are asked as ranges, so the cost is that of the rules and not of the days in the span. Only a rule function must be asked a day at a time, and for that a span of more than 40,000 days (about 110 years, more than any calendar the browser can show is given) counts as blocked.

DayClock.name: DayClock
DayClock.summary: A day round a clock face: one wedge for each of the 24 hours, midnight at the top and running clockwise. A wedge's length is its hour's value (steps, active minutes); its colour is its category (a mood, a kind of activity) or the band of a `ColorScale`; how strong it is says its level. Up to eight moments are marked round the outside with icons, the hour that is now is outlined, and the hub holds the day's total.

constructors.name: new
constructors.doc: A clock called `title`, with no values yet.

methods.name: band
methods.doc: Draws a thin band round the hub, under the wedges, in each hour's category: every hour shows its category, an hour with nothing in it too (asleep, resting), where its wedge is only a faint stub. An hour with no category leaves a gap in the band.

methods.name: values
methods.doc: The value of each hour from midnight, 24 of them: what sets a wedge's length. Fewer leave the rest empty; more are not read. A gap (`None`, NaN) is an hour with no value.

methods.name: levels
methods.doc: How strong each hour is drawn, 0 to 1: how much of the hour was active, say. By default it is the hour's value against the busiest hour's.

methods.name: category
methods.args: name: impl Into<String>, ink: impl Into<Ink>
methods.doc: Adds a category called `name` in `ink`: the next one is numbered after it, from 0. Wedges take theirs from `categories`, and the legend names them.

methods.name: categories
methods.doc: The category of each hour from midnight, by its number: `None` for an hour with none.

methods.name: colors
methods.doc: Colours each hour by the band its value falls in, where it has no category.

methods.name: ink
methods.doc: The colour of an hour with no category or band: chart colour 1 by default.

methods.name: moment
methods.doc: Marks a moment round the outside. Eight are marked at most, in the order given; the table lists every one in its hour.

methods.name: now
methods.doc: Outlines the hour that is now, 0 to 23.

methods.name: max
methods.doc: The value a full-length wedge stands for: the busiest hour's by default.

methods.name: format
methods.doc: How values are written.

methods.name: unit
methods.doc: What the values count, written after them: `steps`, `min`.

methods.name: label
methods.doc: The small capitals under the total in the hub: the unit by default.

methods.name: center_icon
methods.doc: An icon over the total in the hub.

methods.name: center
methods.doc: Puts markup of your own in the hub instead of the total, hidden from assistive technology.

methods.name: hub
methods.doc: The colour the hub is washed with: chart colour 7 by default.

methods.name: size
methods.doc: The widest the drawing grows, in pixels, 200 to 480 (440 by default): it fills a narrower space, so the clock is as wide as its container up to this.

methods.name: size_on

constructors.doc: The flag of a code that comes from data, such as `"in"` or `"GB-SCT"`. A code no flag has draws a neutral placeholder and never panics.

methods.doc: Hides the flag from assistive technology, for when the country's name is written beside it.

methods.name: sprite
methods.doc: Draws the flag as a pointer to a definition made once on the page by a `FlagSprite`, not as its own artwork. A heavy flag is tens of kilobytes (Serbia's is 179 KB), and a table of a hundred rows would repeat it a hundred times; the pointer is about a hundred bytes. The page must hold a `FlagSprite` with this code in it, or the flag is drawn empty. A flag of a code the toolkit does not know is drawn in full, as always.

methods.name: scope
methods.doc: Gives the ids inside the flag's artwork a prefix, so that two copies on one page never share one. Only Anguilla, Belarus and Nicaragua need it: they cut a shape out of their drawing with a clip, and browsers do not draw a clip that is defined inside hidden content. Use it on the flags of a closed menu, a hidden tab or a closed dialog that sit before the same flags in view. A scope is letters, digits, `-` and `_`; anything else is ignored.

Give it to a `DateRangePicker` with `limits` and the browser holds a person to it; give the same value to `DateRangeQuery::checked` and the server holds the request to it. Nothing is said twice, so the two can't differ.

constructors.name: new
constructors.doc: Limits that hold a range to `rules`: both ends and every day between.

methods.name: min_days
methods.doc: The fewest days a range may hold (one at least).

methods.name: max_days
methods.doc: The most days a range may hold (one at least).

methods.name: rules
methods.doc: The days that can't be chosen.

methods.name: least_days
methods.doc: The fewest days a range may hold, when limited.

methods.name: most_days
methods.doc: The most days a range may hold, when limited.

methods.name: check
methods.doc: Why `range` can't be chosen, or `Ok`: the check the browser makes as a range is picked, made again by the server.

RangeScale.name: RangeScale
RangeScale.summary: One value on a scale between a low end and a high end, with a marker: a resting heart rate between 40 and 120, a blood-pressure reading, a price between its day's low and high. The track can be a gradient through any stops, so the ends can read as good and bad; the colours are never the only way to read it, because the end labels, the summary and the table give the numbers.

constructors.name: new
constructors.args: title: impl Into<String>, value: impl IntoValue
constructors.doc: A scale called `title` with the marker at `value`. A value that is missing leaves the chart empty.

methods.name: range
methods.args: min: impl IntoValue, max: impl IntoValue
methods.doc: The low and the high end of the scale (0 and 100 by default). Reversed ends are put in order; ends that are equal make a scale one wide.

methods.name: track
methods.doc: Paints the track with `gradient`, over the quiet track: its stops set where the colours change, along the scale from the low end (0) to the high end (1). Use a horizontal one.

methods.name: format
methods.doc: How the value and the ends are written.

methods.name: ends
methods.args: low: impl Into<String>, high: impl Into<String>
methods.doc: Writes `low` and `high` under the ends, instead of the ends as numbers.

methods.name: show_value
methods.doc: Writes the value above the marker.

methods.name: motion
methods.doc: How the marker comes in: it pops in, after the delay. Off by default; always off for a reader who asks for less motion.

methods.name: words
methods.doc: The words the chart writes besides the common ones.

methods.name: id
methods.doc: Sets the figure's id, which the table switch and the names inside it build on. Give one when two charts on a page share a title.

methods.name: heading
methods.doc: Writes the title as a heading of `level` (2 to 6) rather than a caption.

methods.name: hide_title
methods.doc: Keeps the title for assistive technology and the table's caption, but shows none: for a chart in a card that has the title already.

methods.name: description
methods.doc: A line under the title.

methods.name: summary
methods.doc: Replaces the summary written from the data.

methods.name: show_summary
methods.doc: Shows the summary under the drawing, as well as giving it to assistive technology.

methods.name: labels
methods.doc: The words the chart writes.

methods.name: locale
methods.doc: Writes numbers and dates for a language: `en-IN`, `de`, `fr`, `ar`.

methods.doc: Writes numbers with these marks.

methods.name: date_locale
methods.doc: Writes dates with this locale.

methods.name: loading
methods.doc: Shows a placeholder the height of the chart while its data loads.

methods.name: failed

Reasoning.name: Reasoning
Reasoning.summary: What the assistant thought before it answered, folded, in the reader's words of its choosing: untrusted text, drawn muted.

constructors.name: new

methods.name: open

methods.name: label

Region.name: Region
Region.summary: A named part of a page that updates by itself: fetched after paint, polled, or refetched when an op invalidates it. Its answer morphs in.

constructors.name: new
constructors.doc: A region named `id`.

methods.name: src
methods.doc: Sets where its content comes from: a page holding an element with this id, or a fragment: a `View` whose body is what goes inside, which may hold parts that need the runtime (a lazy tab, another region), since the toolkit marks a view answered to a region's fetch as its fragment. A page with the runtime that lacks this id and isn't marked so (one a proxy serves), or a redirect, is somewhere else: the user goes there, as when a session has ended.

methods.name: lazy
methods.doc: Fetches it after paint, showing a skeleton until then.

methods.name: poll
methods.doc: Refetches it this often, while the page is visible.

methods.name: feed
methods.args: into: impl Into<AttrValue>, after: impl Into<AttrValue>, empty: Option<&str>
methods.doc: Makes it a feed: each poll asks the source for what is newer than a cursor and adds it at the start of the element `into` inside the region, instead of fetching the whole region again.

methods.name: feed_limit
methods.doc: Trims a feed to its newest `most` rows as new ones arrive, so a page left open for days doesn't grow without end. The default is 200, which `0` also means (a feed with no limit is not offered); the most is 5,000. The row the reader is in is never taken out.

methods.name: announce_new
methods.args: many: impl Into<String>, one: impl Into<String>
methods.doc: Announces new feed rows to assistive technology: `many` with `{n}` filled in, or `one` when a single row came. Without this a feed adds rows silently.

methods.name: live_from
methods.doc: Refetches the region whenever this server-sent event stream says something, or, with a feed, asks the source for what is new. Needs `src`.

methods.name: live_on
methods.doc: Refetches the region, or with a feed asks for what is new, whenever its stream says one of its names: the app's live hub (`LiveStream::on`) or any stream on this site. Everything `live_from` says holds; use one or the other. With the hub, a stream that comes back after it dropped is told only what it missed, so the region fetches only if it missed something.

methods.name: live_event
methods.doc: Listens for the stream's events called `name` instead of its unnamed ones (`event: name` on the wire), so one stream can feed several regions. A name of letters, digits and `_ . : -`, at most 64 long; any other is ignored. `open` and `error` are the connection's own events, so they are ignored too. `live_on` takes names made at run time, and several.

methods.name: when_failed
methods.doc: Says `state` when a fetch of the region fails in a way the server did not draw: the connection failed, the request ran out of time, or something between answered in its own words (a proxy's page, an answer that is not HTML). What the region had stays, and the state appears beside it. An error from your app is drawn by the server as a state and shown by the runtime in place of the region (see `ErrorPage`), whether or not you call this.

methods.name: when_offline
methods.doc: `when_failed` with "You're offline" and a Try again button that fetches the region again, shown only when the browser could not reach the server at all (the connection failed). A request that ran out of time, or a server that answered with an error, is not being offline: use `when_failed` with your own words for those.

methods.name: children
methods.doc: Adds its content.

Relation.name: Relation
Relation.summary: How two measures relate: a signed value, whether it is significant, and a note.

constructors.name: new
constructors.doc: A pair that came to `value`, significant until told otherwise. A value that is not a finite number is a pair never tested.

constructors.name: untested
constructors.doc: A pair never tested: too few paired days, say. Drawn almost blank.

methods.name: significant
methods.doc: Whether the value is a real link and not chance. A pair that is not significant is drawn in a neutral tone, whatever its value.

methods.name: note
methods.doc: Words about the pair, shown in its tooltip and its table row: the days it rests on, the test.

RelationList.name: RelationList
RelationList.summary: A ranked list of how pairs of measures relate: the findings of a set of correlations, strongest first. Each row names the pair, writes its signed value, draws a bar from the centre to the right for a link that moves together and to the left for one that moves apart (longer the stronger, to the value at `peak`), and says its note under it.

constructors.name: new
constructors.doc: A list called `title`.

methods.name: relation
methods.args: a: impl Into<String>, b: impl Into<String>, relation: Relation
methods.doc: How measures `a` and `b` relate. The rows are ranked by the size of the value, whatever order they are given in.

methods.name: colors
methods.args: positive: impl Into<Ink>, negative: impl Into<Ink>
methods.doc: The colours of a link that moves together and of one that moves apart: blue and orange by default, which stay apart for every reader. Use tones when the sign means good and bad.

methods.name: peak
methods.doc: The value a bar reaches the end at (1 by default, for a correlation). A larger value is as long as it.

methods.name: format
methods.doc: How values are written (two decimals by default). A value above zero is written with its `+`.

methods.name: value_name
methods.doc: What the value is called in the table (`Value` by default).

methods.name: only_significant
methods.doc: Lists only the significant pairs. The table still has every pair.

methods.name: words
methods.doc: The words the list writes.

methods.name: motion
methods.doc: How the rows come in: each bar grows from the centre, one after another. Off by default.

methods.name: id
methods.doc: Sets the figure's id, which the table switch and the names inside it build on. Give one when two charts on a page share a title.

methods.name: heading
methods.doc: Writes the title as a heading of `level` (2 to 6) rather than a caption.

methods.name: hide_title
methods.doc: Keeps the title for assistive technology and the table's caption, but shows none: for a chart in a card that has the title already.

methods.doc: Shows the summary under the drawing, as well as giving it to assistive technology.

methods.name: failed

Reply.name: Reply
Reply.summary: What an action handler answers: ops for the runtime, and what a browser with JavaScript off gets instead.

constructors.name: redirect
constructors.doc: Goes to `href`, on this site. A URL that would leave it (`//host`, `/\\host`, `https://host`) goes nowhere, so a `next` from a request can't send a user away. To leave on purpose, use `redirect_external`.

constructors.name: ops_or_redirect
constructors.doc: Applies ops; with JavaScript off, goes to `href`.

constructors.name: redirect_external
constructors.doc: Goes to `href`, which may be on another site: a sign-in provider, a payment page. Never give this a URL from a request unchecked: that is an open redirect.

constructors.name: view
constructors.doc: Applies ops; with JavaScript off, shows `view`.

constructors.name: ops
constructors.doc: Applies ops; with JavaScript off, answers 204.

methods.name: op
methods.doc: Adds an op.

methods.name: morph
methods.args: target: impl Into<String>, node: impl Into<Node>
methods.doc: Morphs element `target` into `node`.

methods.name: toast
methods.doc: Adds a toast. With JavaScript off, the next page shows it.

methods.name: toast_with
methods.doc: Adds a toast with a title, an action, a name or a time of its own. With JavaScript off, the next page shows its tone and text.

methods.name: status
methods.doc: Sets the status of the ops response.

constructors.name: new
constructors.doc: A report over `range` at `grain`, in `zone`. A grain that would cut the window into more than `MAX_BUCKETS` periods gives way to the finest one that doesn't (`grain` says which), and a window too long even for years keeps its last 400 (`cut` says so).

constructors.name: from_query
constructors.args: query: &ReportQuery, limits: &RangeRules, today: NaiveDate, default: DatePreset, zone: &Tz
constructors.doc: The report a request asks for: its window when `limits` allow it, `default` counted from `today` when the URL has none or one they refuse (which `refused` then says), and its grain when it fits.

constructors.name: from_query_starting
constructors.args: query: &ReportQuery, limits: &RangeRules, today: NaiveDate, default: DatePreset, week_start: Weekday, zone: &Tz
constructors.doc: `from_query` with weeks starting on `week_start`.

methods.name: zone
methods.doc: The IANA name of the zone the periods are in, from the zone itself; `None` for a fixed offset other than UTC.

methods.name: range
methods.doc: The window counted: the one asked for, or its last 400 years when it was longer than that (see `cut`).

methods.name: cut
methods.doc: The window asked for, when it was too long to count by years and was cut to its last 400: the page should say so.

methods.name: grain
methods.doc: The period the window is cut into: the grain asked for, or a coarser one when that would have made more than `MAX_BUCKETS` periods.

methods.name: asked_grain
methods.doc: The grain asked for, before the limit on periods.

methods.name: auto_grain
methods.doc: The grain the window's length picks.

methods.name: week_start
methods.doc: The first day of a week.

methods.name: buckets
methods.doc: The periods, in order.

methods.name: bounds
methods.doc: The instants the window covers, `[start, end)`: what a query filters on.

methods.name: refused
methods.doc: Why the window in the URL was not used, when it was refused.

methods.name: from_url
methods.doc: Whether the window came from the URL (not the default).

methods.name: grains
methods.doc: The grains a person may switch to: those that draw between 2 and `MAX_BUCKETS` periods of this window.

methods.name: params
methods.doc: The URL's parameters for this window and grain: what a link keeps. The grain is left out when it is the one the window picks by itself.

methods.name: href
methods.doc: `path` with this report's parameters, and `grain` instead of its own when given.

methods.name: picker
methods.doc: The range picker for this window, named `from` and `to`, with the report's rules and today: put it in a GET form with the grain as a hidden field, and give the form `autocomplete="off"`, or Back brings the dates back as they were typed rather than as the page was drawn.

methods.name: times
methods.doc: The periods' starts, for `Chart::times`.

methods.name: chart
methods.doc: A chart over this report's periods: `chart` with its times and grain set.

methods.name: bucket_of
methods.doc: The period an instant falls in.

methods.name: count
methods.doc: How many of `instants` fall in each period: for data already in memory.

methods.name: sum
methods.doc: The sum of the values in each period: for data already in memory.

methods.name: series
methods.doc: A series over the periods, from counts.

methods.name: grain_links
methods.doc: The grain switch: a link per grain this window can take, the current one marked.

methods.name: measure
methods.args: query: Builder<M>, time: impl Into<TimeColumn>, metric: Metric, exec: &E
methods.doc: `metric` in each period of the report, over `query` (the app's scoped query) with its rows' instants in `time`. A column of seconds or milliseconds since 1970 is named with `TimeColumn::UnixSeconds` or `TimeColumn::UnixMillis`.

methods.name: measure_with
methods.args: query: Builder<M>, time: impl Into<TimeColumn>, metric: Metric, bucketing: Bucketing, exec: &E
methods.doc: `measure`, choosing how the periods are found.

methods.name: measure_by
methods.args: query: Builder<M>, time: impl Into<TimeColumn>, group: &'static str, groups: &[&str], metric: Metric, exec: &E
methods.doc: `metric` per value of `group` in each period: one series per name in `groups`, in that order, and one more for every other value, NULL included (Other). At most seven names are counted on their own, as a chart draws eight series: the rest are counted in Other. On an SQL database this is one grouped query.

methods.name: measure_rows
methods.args: query: Builder<M>, time: impl Into<TimeColumn>, key: &'static str, keys: &[Value], metric: Metric, exec: &E
methods.doc: `metric` in each period for each of `keys`, a value of the column `key`: one series per key, in that order, from one grouped query. This is how a page of a table gets the series behind a `Sparkline::cell` in each row without a query per row: give the ids on the page, as the `Value` the column holds (`Value::I64(id)` for a bigint, `Value::String(..)` for a text or uuid column). Rows of any other key count nowhere. At most 500 keys are taken; more is an error, as a page is never longer.

methods.name: table
methods.doc: The report's numbers as a table. `period_header` heads the first column; each of `series` is a name and its values, one for each period, in the order the report's `measure` gives them. A series shorter than the report is filled with gaps, and a longer one is cut.

methods.name: drill_links
methods.doc: A link for each period to the page that lists the rows behind it: `path` with a range filter on `column` for the days the period covers, in the grammar a `DataTable` reads (`filter[created_at][gte]=2026-11-02&filter[created_at][lte]=2026-11-08`). An hour or a minute is listed with its whole day. Give them to `Chart::drill`. A column that is not a plain name (letters, digits and `_`) gives no links.

methods.name: previous
methods.doc: The window just before this one, as many days long, in the same zone and grain: the period to compare with. A window of seven days from the 8th has the seven days from the 1st. Pass the zone this report was cut in.

methods.name: previous_series
methods.doc: The previous window's figures as a series of this report's periods, drawn in the quiet ink: the period before, beside the one on show. `previous_values` are what `measure` gave for `previous`; they are laid on this report's periods by position (the first period against the first), a shorter run leaving gaps and a longer one cut.

ReportQuery.name: ReportQuery
ReportQuery.summary: What a report reads from its URL: `from` and `to` (the window, both days included) and `grain` (`hour`, `day`, `week`, `month`). A key that comes twice keeps its first value; anything else is ignored.

methods.name: window
methods.doc: The window, as the range picker's query reads it.

ReturnTo.name: ReturnTo
ReturnTo.summary: An address on this site that is safe to send a user to.

constructors.name: parse
constructors.doc: Checks `raw`. `None` when it could lead anywhere but this site.

constructors.name: parse_for
constructors.doc: Checks `raw` and also refuses the sign-in page itself, and anything below it, which would send the user round in a circle. `sign_in` is its address; the two are compared as a server reads them, with their escapes decoded (`/%73ign-in` is `/sign-in`). A `sign_in` that is not a path on this site (a provider's address) refuses nothing.

constructors.name: of_uri
constructors.doc: The page a request asked for: its path and query. `None` when that could not be sent back safely, such as a path with a backslash in it.

constructors.name: from_query
constructors.doc: The `next` of a query string (`a=1&next=%2Fdeals`), checked.

constructors.name: resolve
constructors.doc: Where to go after signing in: `next` when it is safe, else `fallback`, which is yours and must also be on this site (anything else becomes `#`).

constructors.name: resolve_for
constructors.doc: `resolve` that also drops the sign-in page at `sign_in` (see `parse_for`): what a sign-in handler should use.

methods.name: as_str
methods.doc: The address.

methods.name: into_local
methods.doc: The address as a redirect target.

methods.name: sign_in_href
methods.doc: `sign_in` with this address as its `next`: `/sign-in?next=%2Fdeals%2F42`.

Rgb.name: Rgb
Rgb.summary: An sRGB colour, eight bits a channel. There is no alpha: contrast is undefined for a colour you can see through.

constructors.name: hex
constructors.doc: The colour `0xrrggbb`.

constructors.name: parse
constructors.doc: Reads `#rgb`, `#rrggbb` (any case) or `rgb(r, g, b)` with whole numbers from 0 to 255, commas or spaces between them. Nothing else: no names, no alpha, no other functions, no escapes. Spaces around the colour are ignored.

constructors.name: from_oklab
constructors.doc: The colour at an OKLab point, or `None` when the point is outside sRGB.

constructors.name: from_oklch
constructors.doc: The colour at lightness `l`, chroma `c` and hue `h` (degrees) in OKLCH, with the chroma lowered until it fits in sRGB.

methods.name: to_u32
methods.doc: The colour as `0xrrggbb`.

methods.name: to_hex
methods.doc: `#rrggbb`, lower case: the only way a colour is written into CSS.

methods.name: write_hex
methods.doc: Writes `to_hex` into `out`.

methods.name: luminance
methods.doc: The relative luminance, from 0 (black) to 1 (white), as WCAG 2 defines it.

methods.name: contrast
methods.doc: The WCAG 2 contrast ratio with `other`, from 1 to 21.

methods.name: to_oklab
methods.doc: The colour in OKLab: lightness from 0 to 1, then the two axes.

methods.name: to_oklch
methods.doc: The colour in OKLCH: lightness, chroma and hue in degrees.

methods.name: mix
methods.doc: `self` mixed with `other` in OKLab: `0.0` is `self`, `1.0` is `other`.

methods.name: over
methods.doc: `self` at `alpha` (0 to 1) laid over `under`, as a browser composites: in sRGB.

methods.name: until_contrast
methods.doc: `self` moved toward `toward` in OKLab, in steps of 2 %, until it reaches `ratio` against every colour of `on`. `toward` itself when no step does.

methods.name: vivid
methods.doc: The far end of a chart colour's sheen, and the colour of a ring's second lap, on the `side` palette: the same colour deeper on a light page and brighter on a dark one. It keeps its colour as it changes: deeper is darker with a little more chroma, and a warm hue (orange, amber, yellow) turns a little toward red as it darkens, the way pigments deepen, so it never turns brown, as a mix with the text's near-black would. Brighter is lighter, a touch less vivid, warm hues a touch toward yellow.

methods.name: ink
methods.doc: The text to put on a fill of this colour: white wherever white reaches 4.5:1, otherwise a deep shade of the fill's own hue, which never reads as plain black on a bright colour.

methods.doc: Shows a placeholder the height of the chart while its data loads.

methods.name: failed

methods.name: empty
methods.doc: What an empty chart says: a heading and a line under it.

methods.name: action
methods.doc: Something beside the title: a link to the full report, a menu.

methods.name: attr
methods.doc: Sets an attribute on the figure.

methods.name: max
methods.doc: The top of the scale: the goal the value is measured against (100 by default). A value past it draws a second lap on a ring.

methods.name: format
methods.doc: How the value is written in the middle, the summary and the table.

methods.name: unit
methods.doc: What the value counts, written after it: `%`, `kcal`, `bpm`. A word gets a space before it; a sign such as `%` or `°C` doesn't.

methods.name: ink
methods.doc: Colours the arc with any `Ink` of the theme.

methods.name: tone
methods.doc: Colours the arc by what it means.

methods.name: fill
methods.doc: Paints the arc with `gradient`, which spans the whole ring, so the colour moves round it. `Ink::own` in its stops is the arc's own colour: `Gradient::sheen(Ink::own())` turns it brighter along the diagonal.

methods.name: colors
methods.doc: Colours the arc by the band its value falls in. The thresholds are values in the scale's own units, as a chart series reads them: on a gauge from 0 to 2, `from(1.3, ..)` starts a band at 1.3. The band's label is said in the summary and the table, so the colour is never alone.

methods.name: track
methods.doc: What the track under the arc is drawn in: a faint grey (the default), a faint tint of the arc's colour, or nothing.

methods.name: glow
methods.doc: Puts a soft glow of its own colour around the arc.

methods.name: halo
methods.doc: Draws a thin halo ring just outside the track, in the arc's colour or gradient.

methods.name: label
methods.doc: Small capitals under the value: what it is, such as `Sleep score`. Under a ring smaller than 96 pixels it is written under the ring. It also names the row of the table.

methods.name: center_icon

methods.name: center_none

variants.name: Tinted

constructors.name: from_query
constructors.doc: Reads the open branches from a query string. Other fields of the query stay in the links, within limits: every caret repeats them, so at most 200 open branches of 256 bytes each and 2 KiB in all are kept, and at most 20 other fields and 1 KiB of them; what does not fit is left out of the links.

methods.name: param
methods.doc: Names the field the open branches are kept in (`open` by default). Call it before reading: it re-reads `query`.

methods.name: is_open
methods.doc: Whether the branch `id` is open.

methods.name: open_ids
methods.doc: The open branches.

methods.name: toggled
methods.doc: The address with `id` opened, or closed if it was open.

Trend.name: Trend
Trend.summary: Which way something moved and by how much: an arrow, the change with its sign, and the colour of what it means. Whether a rise is good news depends on the figure: more steps are good, a higher resting heart rate is not, so the colour follows `up_is_bad` and never the direction alone. The words "Up", "Down" or "No change" are read by a screen reader before the figure.

constructors.name: new
constructors.doc: A change of `change`, written with its sign and a percent sign: `12.4` is `+12.4%`. Use `suffix` for another unit.

methods.name: up_is_bad
methods.doc: A rise is bad news (resting heart rate, stress, debt): it is coloured as a warning, and a fall as good.

methods.name: tone
methods.doc: Colours the trend with `tone` whichever way it moved: `Tone::Neutral` shows the direction with no judgement.

methods.name: decimals
methods.doc: The most decimals written, 0 to 3 (1 by default).

methods.name: suffix
methods.doc: What follows the number: `%` by default, ` bpm`, ` min`.

methods.name: locale
methods.doc: Writes the number for a language: `de`, `en-IN`.

methods.name: words
methods.args: up: impl Into<Cow<'static, str>>, down: impl Into<Cow<'static, str>>, none: impl Into<Cow<'static, str>>
methods.doc: The words a screen reader hears before the figure.

Upload.name: Upload
Upload.summary: A file field with a drop area, a list of the files and, in a form of its own, progress.

constructors.name: new
constructors.args: name: impl Into<String>, label: impl Into<Node>
constructors.doc: A field posting its files as `name`, called `label`.

methods.name: id
methods.doc: Sets the id (`upload-{name}` otherwise). The file input's is `{id}-input`.

methods.name: action
methods.doc: Makes the upload a form of its own that posts to `href`.

methods.name: csrf
methods.doc: Puts the session's CSRF token in the form as the field `_csrf`, which a post with no script sends. The module sends the token it finds in the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie. A field inside a form of yours leaves the token to that form.

methods.name: limits
methods.doc: Sets what is accepted. The default is ten megabytes, one file, any kind.

methods.name: labels
methods.doc: Sets the words.

methods.name: manual
methods.doc: Waits for the Send button instead of sending a file as soon as it is chosen.

methods.name: chunks
methods.doc: Sends large files in chunks through `url`, an address on this site that is served by `Uploads::begin` and its companions. Anything that is not an address on this site is ignored.

methods.name: send_to
methods.doc: Inside a form of yours: the module sends each chosen file at once to `url`, an address on this site whose route stores it and answers with its key (`Received::into_keyed_response`), and puts the key in a hidden field named like the upload, which the form posts in place of the file. With no script the file goes with the form, which must be a multipart form. Anything that is not an address on this site is ignored.

methods.name: key
methods.doc: The key of a file already sent (`file_key`), which the form posts again: for a form drawn again after it was refused, so the file is not chosen twice. The field is then not required in the browser.

methods.name: chunk_from
methods.doc: Sets how large a file must be to go in chunks (8 MB by default).

methods.name: refresh
methods.doc: Names a region (by its id) to fetch again when files have been sent, so the list it draws shows them.

methods.name: hint
methods.doc: Adds a line after the limits.

methods.name: error
methods.doc: Shows an error under the drop area and marks the field invalid.

methods.name: required
methods.doc: Marks the field required.

methods.name: disabled
methods.doc: Disables the field.

methods.name: compact
methods.doc: A smaller drop area, for a form with little room.

methods.name: previews
methods.doc: Shows a small picture of each chosen file that is a picture (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or AVIF, up to 2 MB), before it is sent. The browser reads the file into a `data:` address, which the page's content security policy allows where it allows no `blob:`; a file that is larger, or another kind, is listed with its name only. A file the server already has gets its picture from `UploadedFile::thumbnail`.

methods.name: file
methods.doc: Lists a file the server already has.

methods.name: files
methods.doc: Lists the files the server already has.

UploadLabels.name: UploadLabels
UploadLabels.summary: Every word an upload says: on the page, in the browser module and in the server's refusals. The defaults are English. A word with `{name}`, `{max}`, `{types}` or `{count}` in it gets that value; a word without one is plain text.

UploadLimits.name: UploadLimits
UploadLimits.summary: What an upload accepts. The page shows these as hints and the server holds every file to them, so a browser that ignores the hints, or is not a browser, gets the same answer.

constructors.name: new
constructors.doc: Files of at most `max_bytes` bytes (at least one), one file, any kind.

constructors.name: size_text
constructors.doc: A size in words: `800 B`, `1.5 KB`, `10 KB`, `2 MB`, `1.5 GB`. Binary units, and no `.0`. The browser module writes sizes the same way.

methods.name: max_files
methods.doc: Allows `files` files in one send: at least one, at most 100.

methods.name: accept
methods.doc: Adds the kinds of file that are accepted: MIME types such as `image/png` and wildcards such as `image/*`. An entry that is neither is dropped. With none, any kind is accepted. The kind is read from the file's first bytes, never from its name or from what the client says it is.

methods.name: bytes
methods.doc: The largest file, in bytes.

methods.name: files
methods.doc: The most files in one send.

methods.name: types
methods.doc: The accepted kinds, lower case. Empty means any.

methods.name: allows
methods.doc: Whether a file of type `mime` is accepted.

methods.name: types_text
methods.doc: The kinds in words: `PNG or JPG`, `PDF, images or CSV`. Empty when any kind is accepted.

methods.name: sentence
methods.doc: The limits as one sentence for the hint: `PNG or JPG, up to 2 MB, up to 5 files`.

methods.name: rules
methods.doc: The same limits as navree-storage's upload rules, which hold a file to them while it is written.

UploadedFile.name: UploadedFile
UploadedFile.summary: A file the server already has, as a row of the list: its name, its size, a link to it and, when you give an address for it, a button that removes it.

constructors.name: new
constructors.doc: A file called `name`. The name is text to show and nothing else.

methods.name: size
methods.doc: Shows its size.

methods.name: href
methods.doc: Links the name to the file.

methods.name: thumbnail
methods.doc: Shows a small picture of the file before its name: an address on this site that serves a picture (the page's content security policy allows no other). Anything that is not an address on this site is ignored. The picture has no description: the name beside it says what the file is.

methods.name: remove
methods.doc: Adds a Remove button that posts to `href`, through the page's one post form. It works with no script, and the page then loads the core runtime for the post.

methods.name: row
methods.doc: The row, in `labels`' words.

Uploads.name: Uploads
Uploads.summary: Receives the files an `Upload` sends, into a directory of a navree-storage disk, holding every file to its `UploadLimits`.

constructors.name: new
constructors.args: disk: Disk, dir: impl Into<String>, limits: UploadLimits
constructors.doc: Files go to `dir` on `disk`, under random names, and are held to `limits`.

methods.name: labels
methods.doc: Sets the words of the refusals.

methods.name: chunk_bytes
methods.doc: Sets the size of a part: between 64 KB and 16 MB, and large enough that the largest file has at most 4,096 parts.

methods.name: chunk_ttl
methods.doc: Sets how long an unfinished chunked upload is kept (a day by default).

methods.name: chunk_sessions
methods.doc: Sets how many chunked uploads one owner may have unfinished at once: at least one, 16 by default. `begin` refuses another (`too_many`) until one is finished, aborted or has expired, so nobody fills the disk with parts of files that never end.

methods.name: limits
methods.doc: The limits.

methods.name: body_limit
methods.doc: The body limit for the route that `receive`s: the largest file and a little more for the rest of the form.

methods.name: chunk_body_limit
methods.doc: The body limit for the route that takes a part: the size of a part.

methods.name: receive
methods.doc: Reads the files of `form` and stores the ones inside the limits. A file that breaks a limit is refused by name and the rest go on; a form that cannot be read at all, or that is larger than the route allows, is an error, and what the request stored is taken back.

methods.name: receive_into
methods.doc: Like `receive`, keeping at most `room` files: for an app that counts the files a person has stored and allows more only while there is room.

methods.name: respond
methods.args: received: Received, headers: &HeaderMap, back: impl Into<LocalHref>
methods.doc: The answer to a request: JSON for the browser module, and for a post with no script a redirect to `back` with a toast, in this upload's words.

methods.name: begin
methods.doc: Starts a chunked upload for `owner`, who is whoever the app says is sending: a user's id. Only that owner can send its parts and finish it. The file's size is held to the limit here, before a byte is sent, and the owner to its `chunk_sessions`: the begins of one owner take turns, so a burst of them cannot open more. The owner is one person: for a guest, pass something of that guest's own (its session's id), never one name for every guest, who would then share those uploads.

methods.name: put_chunk
methods.args: owner: &str, id: &str, index: u32, body: Bytes
methods.doc: Keeps part number `index` (from 0) of the upload `id`. Parts may come in any order and a part may come twice: the last one sent stays. Every part but the last is exactly the size `begin` named; the last is what is left.

methods.name: finish
methods.doc: Puts the parts of the upload `id` together, once every one is here, and stores the file. The kind is read from the file's first bytes with the sniffer a plain post uses, and a file of a kind that is not accepted is thrown away with its parts.

methods.name: abort
methods.doc: Stops the upload `id` and removes its parts. It waits for a `finish` of the same upload that is under way.

methods.name: sweep
methods.doc: Removes the parts of uploads that were not finished in time, and returns how many uploads that was. `begin` does this, a few hundred at a time; an app with many uploads can also run it from a schedule.

UserMenu.name: UserMenu
UserMenu.summary: The user at the foot of the sidebar: an avatar, name and email, and a menu.

constructors.name: new
constructors.args: name: impl Into<Cow<'static, str>>, email: impl Into<Cow<'static, str>>
constructors.doc: The user `name`.

methods.name: link
methods.args: label: impl Into<Cow<'static, str>>, href: impl Into<Href>
methods.doc: Adds a link to the menu, for a page to read. It isn't fetched ahead of a click. Something that changes state, such as signing out, is an `action`.

methods.name: action
methods.args: label: impl Into<Cow<'static, str>>, href: impl Into<Href>
methods.doc: Adds a button that posts to `href`: signing out, switching workspace. It works with JavaScript off, carrying the session's token as a field when there is one.

constructors.name: new
constructors.doc: A wizard with no steps. `id` names it in the page and tells two wizards on one page apart.

methods.name: base
methods.doc: Sets where the wizard's pages are: a step is at `{base}/{draft id}/{step id}`.

methods.name: step
methods.doc: Adds a step. A step whose id another has gets a number added to it, and the id `review` is taken by the review step. At most 100 steps are kept.

methods.name: review
methods.doc: Ends with a review: every step's answers as text, each with a button that opens that step, and the Finish button.

methods.name: free
methods.doc: Lets the steps be done in any order. The last step still checks them all.

methods.name: vertical
methods.doc: Stacks the stepper on the side.

methods.name: no_leave
methods.doc: Leaves out the Save and leave button.

methods.name: labels
methods.doc: Sets the words.

methods.name: stepper_labels
methods.doc: Sets the words of the stepper.

methods.name: language
methods.doc: Sets the language the steps are checked in: the app's validation messages and the reader's date, time and slider words (`Language::of(ctx)` reads both for a request). Without it the steps say their errors in English. The wizard is cheap to build, so an app builds it for each request.

methods.name: url
methods.doc: The address of a step of a draft.

methods.name: start
methods.doc: A new draft on the first step.

methods.name: draft
methods.doc: A new draft on the first step with an id of your own (see `Draft::with_id`).

methods.name: len
methods.doc: How many steps there are, the review included.

methods.name: is_empty
methods.doc: Whether there are none.

methods.name: entry
methods.doc: The step to open for a draft: where the person was, if it can be reached, else the last step that can.

methods.name: states
methods.doc: The state of every step, the way the stepper shows them, with `current` the open one.

methods.name: submit
methods.doc: What a post meant. Changes `draft` as it says; save it when `WizardOutcome::changed`.

methods.name: page
methods.doc: A page for a step of a draft. The step must be one the draft can reach.

WizardAction.name: WizardAction
WizardAction.summary: What a post to a wizard asks for: the value of its `_wizard` field.

constructors.name: parse
constructors.doc: Reads a `_wizard` field. Anything else is `None`.

variants.name: Next
variants.doc: Check this step and open the next.

variants.name: Back
variants.doc: Keep what was typed and open the step before.

variants.name: Save
variants.doc: Keep what was typed and leave; the draft waits.

variants.name: Goto
variants.doc: Keep what was typed and open the step with this id.

WizardLabels.name: WizardLabels
WizardLabels.summary: The words a wizard writes. English by default.

WizardOutcome.name: WizardOutcome
WizardOutcome.summary: What a post meant, once the wizard has changed the draft.

methods.name: changed
methods.doc: Whether the draft changed, so it must be saved.

variants.name: Invalid
variants.doc: A step has something to fix: open it, and its errors are there.

variants.name: Done
variants.doc: Every step is valid and the draft is submitted. Create what the wizard was for, then discard the draft.

variants.name: Stale
variants.doc: The form was drawn from an older revision: another window changed the draft. Nothing was changed. Draw the draft as it is, with a notice.

WizardPage.name: WizardPage
WizardPage.summary: A step of a wizard, ready to draw.

methods.name: csrf
methods.doc: Puts the session's token in the form, for a post with JavaScript off.

methods.name: notice
methods.doc: Shows a notice above the step.

methods.name: stale
methods.doc: Shows the wizard's notice for a draft changed elsewhere (a `WizardOutcome::Stale`).

methods.name: title_text
methods.doc: The step's title as text, for the page's `<title>`.

WizardStep.name: WizardStep
WizardStep.summary: One step of a `Wizard`. Make one with `WizardStep::of`.

constructors.name: of
constructors.args: id: impl Into<String>, title: impl Into<Node>
constructors.doc: A step whose fields and rules are the struct `T`'s.

WizardStepOf.name: WizardStepOf
WizardStepOf.summary: A step being described: the form it is, and how it is shown. Turns into a `WizardStep` where a wizard takes one.

methods.name: description
methods.doc: A line under the step's title.

methods.name: optional
methods.doc: Lets the step be skipped: it needn't be visited, but if it holds an answer, however the person left it (Next, Back, the stepper or Save), the answer must be valid.

methods.name: form
methods.args: shape: impl Fn(FormView<T>) -> FormView<T> + Send + Sync + 'static
methods.doc: Shapes the step's form: its choices from the database, the dates' locale and the like.
